title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: A low price-to-book multiple is not cheap if depreciation and interest consume sixty percent of operating cash flow.
epigraph.author: Institutional Desk Note

web_blocks.html: At the November 13, 2026 NSE ledger close of ₹778.90, ZF Steering Gear commands a market cap of ₹706.70 Cr across 90.73 lakh shares [8, 23]. Adding consolidated borrowings of ₹165 Cr as of September 2026 puts Enterprise Value (EV) at roughly ₹845 Cr [8]. Against trailing twelve-month (TTM) consolidated sales of ₹645 Cr, the stock trades at 1.31x EV/Sales and 1.40x book value (₹557 per share) [8].

Why does a 90% domestic M&HCV steering duopoly with +53% YoY Q2 FY27 sales growth trade at 1.40x book value? The answer sits in Chapter 6's depreciation and return-on-capital math. Consolidated ROCE is 6.48% and ROE is 3.29%, while free cash flow stayed negative in FY24 (-₹55 Cr), FY25 (-₹19 Cr), and FY26 (-₹11 Cr) [8]. Also, TTM net profit included ₹23 Cr of non-operating Other Income (₹15 Cr in Q1 FY27), while FY26 actual depreciation ran at ₹47 Cr [8].

web_blocks.caption: ZFSTEERING Valuation & Reverse DCF Expectations Bridge (as of 13 Nov 2026)
web_blocks.explanatory_p: Using FY26 actual depreciation of ₹47 Cr (rising to ₹50 Cr as ₹103 Cr CWIP capitalizes) and ₹14 Cr interest, even ₹810 Cr FY28E sales at 12.5% OPM (₹101.25 Cr EBITDA) yields only ₹37.25 Cr PBT and ₹27.94 Cr core PAT (₹30.79/share). Valuing ₹101.25 Cr FY28E EBITDA at 8.5x EV/EBITDA less ₹140 Cr net debt produces a ₹795 Base-Case fair value—just +2.1% above the ₹778.90 close.

web_blocks.html: This depreciation-adjusted bridge exposes why the stock lacks a margin of safety at ₹778.90. Even if DriveSys scales revenue to ₹810 Cr, ₹50 Cr of annual depreciation and ₹14 Cr of interest consume over 60% of operating EBITDA. As a result, core PAT remains modest at ₹27.94 Cr, leaving little room for multiple expansion.

web_blocks.title: FY28E Base-Case Fair Value Estimate (₹795 / Share)
web_blocks.the_number: We estimate FY28E Base-Case Fair Value at ₹795 per share (+2.1% above the ₹778.90 close).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We project FY28E sales at ₹810 Cr and 12.5% OPM to get ₹101.25 Cr EBITDA. Subtracting ₹50 Cr depreciation (reflecting ₹47 Cr FY26 D&A plus ₹103 Cr CWIP) and ₹14 Cr interest gives ₹37.25 Cr PBT, or ₹27.94 Cr core PAT at 25% tax. Applying 8.5x FY28E EV/EBITDA (₹860.6 Cr EV) less ₹140 Cr net debt yields ₹720.6 Cr equity value, or ₹795 per share.
web_blocks.the_inputs: TTM sales ₹645 Cr [8], FY26 D&A ₹47 Cr [8], CWIP ₹103 Cr [8], borrowings ₹165 Cr [8], and 2026-11-13 ledger close ₹778.90.
web_blocks.the_range: In the Bear case (₹557), CV demand stalls and negative FCF pins the stock at 1.0x book value (₹557). In the Bull case (₹1,050), ₹920 Cr sales at 14% OPM (₹128.8 Cr EBITDA, ₹48.6 Cr core PAT) supports 10.0x EV/EBITDA.
web_blocks.if_off: If DriveSys achieves 15%+ OPM or capex drops sharply without raising depreciation above ₹45 Cr, core PAT would beat ₹40 Cr and lift fair value above ₹950.

web_blocks.caption: Listed Indian Auto-Component & Steering Peer Comparison (13 Nov 2026 Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: ZFSTEERING is the smallest name in the peer group and carries the lowest ROCE (6.48%) and ROE (3.29%) compared with Jamna Auto (26.0% ROCE) and Rane Madras (14.0% ROCE).

web_blocks.html: The peer table confirms why ZFSTEERING trades at 1.40x book value. Its 6.48% ROCE trails Jamna Auto (26.0% ROCE) and Rane Madras (14.0% ROCE) [8, 23]. Until CWIP converts into double-digit ROCE, the market will not pay a peer-group earnings multiple.

web_blocks.mechanism: Heavy debt-funded capex in commercial-vehicle forgings compressed ROCE into single digits and kept the stock near 1.2x–1.5x book value until capacity utilization crossed 75% and FCF turned positive.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: ROCE recovered from ~7% in FY20 to >18% by FY23 as revenue scaled from ₹1,216 Cr to ₹3,193 Cr, driving a >4x equity re-rating once deleveraging began.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: ZFSTEERING's 1.40x P/B multiple will not re-rate on revenue growth alone; it requires positive FCF and double-digit ROCE after depreciation.

web_blocks.html: Valuation Trigger: Fair value stays capped near ₹795 until consolidated core PAT (ex-Other Income) clears ₹40 Cr and FCF turns positive. Sustained OPM >= 14% with falling net debt would trigger an upward re-rating.

Sensitivity testing around our ₹795.00 Base-Case fair value confirms how sensitive equity value is to asset turns. Each 100 bps of operating margin on ₹810 Cr sales adds ₹8.1 Cr of EBITDA, or ₹6.08 Cr after tax. Yet ₹50 Cr of annual depreciation still absorbs nearly half of operating profit.

Comparing enterprise multiples across Indian auto-ancillary peers reinforces this conclusion. Jamna Auto earns 26.0% ROCE and Rane Madras earns 14.0% ROCE, whereas ZFSTEERING earns 6.48% ROCE [8, 23]. At ₹778.90 (1.40x book value), the market already prices in a solid operational recovery.
At ₹778.90, book value per share (₹557) provides a cyclical floor, not a catalyst. Without double-digit ROCE, valuation stays anchored near 1.4x book.
In short, ₹778.90 leaves zero margin for error. Until core PAT exceeds ₹40 Cr, we pass.

book_paragraphs: Now that you and I have completed our price-blind audit of the factory floor and ten years of cash flows, we open the market ledger. On November 13, 2026, ZF Steering Gear closed at ₹778.90 on the NSE, valuing the equity at ₹706.70 Cr and enterprise value at roughly ₹845 Cr.

At 1.40 times book value, the stock looks inexpensive at first glance. Yet when we build an honest FY28 earnings bridge using actual FY26 depreciation of ₹47 Cr—rising toward ₹50 Cr once ₹103 Cr of capital work-in-progress goes live—the math tightens sharply.

Even if consolidated sales reach ₹810 Cr at a 12.5 percent operating margin, ₹101.25 Cr of EBITDA leaves just ₹27.94 Cr of core net profit after ₹50 Cr of depreciation, ₹14 Cr of interest, and 25 percent tax. At 8.5 times FY28 EBITDA, fair value sits at ₹795 per share—barely 2 percent above today's close.

When a company's depreciation bill consumes half of its operating profit, patience is your strongest ally. Wait for the cash flow statement to prove that DriveSys can carry its fixed asset base before paying an expansion multiple.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Understate Depreciation
book_callouts.text: When a manufacturer carries ₹103 Cr of CWIP and ₹47 Cr of trailing depreciation, modeling lower D&A creates phantom earnings. Always test forward PAT against actual asset intensity.

book_subsections.title: Benchmarking Against Jamna Auto, Rane, JTEKT, and Sona BLW
paragraphs: When we compare ZF Steering Gear against Jamna Auto, Rane Madras, JTEKT India, and Sona BLW, the capital-efficiency gap stands out. Jamna Auto earns 26.0 percent ROCE, and Rane Madras earns 14.0 percent ROCE, compared with ZF Steering Gear's 6.48 percent.
Until DriveSys converts its Supa investment into higher asset turns and free cash flow, the market has little reason to award a compounder multiple.

book_subsections.title: Weighing Valuation Downside Against Upside
paragraphs: Our Bear case sits at ₹557 per share (1.0 times book value, down 28.5 percent), our Base case sits at ₹795 (up 2.1 percent), and our Bull case sits at ₹1,050 (up 34.8 percent). That leaves expected value at ₹799.25—nearly flat to today's ₹778.90 quote.
In short, the current price already discounts a healthy operational recovery without leaving an asymmetric margin of safety.

book_subsections.title: Why Depreciation Changes the Entire Equity Story
paragraphs: Many investors look only at operating profit before depreciation and assume a growing factory will automatically mint cash. In capital-intensive manufacturing, however, depreciation is not a harmless accounting entry—it represents real wear and tear on expensive extrusion presses, CNC machining centres, and heat-treatment furnaces that must eventually be replaced.

When ZF Steering Gear spent ₹109 Cr in FY26 and accumulated ₹103 Cr of capital work-in-progress, it locked in higher annual depreciation for years to come. Until DriveSys generates enough revenue and gross margin to clear ₹50 Cr of annual depreciation and ₹14 Cr of interest comfortably, net profit per share will remain constrained near ₹30–₹35.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity to Margins and Capital Turns
paragraphs: Let us test what happens if DriveSys Systems performs slightly better or slightly worse than our Base-Case model. Every one-percentage-point change in consolidated operating margin on ₹810 Cr of FY28 sales shifts pre-tax profit by ₹8.1 Cr, or roughly ₹6.70 per share after tax.

That sensitivity cuts both ways. If operating margins reach 14 percent instead of 12.5 percent, core net profit rises toward ₹37 Cr and fair value moves above ₹900. Conversely, if commercial vehicle demand softens and margins slip to 9.5 percent, ₹50 Cr of depreciation and ₹14 Cr of interest push core earnings into a slight loss, pulling the stock back toward its ₹557 tangible book value floor.
Because ₹778.90 sits only 2.1 percent below our ₹795 Base-Case estimate while carrying 28.5 percent downside to ₹557, the risk-reward balance does not justify committing fresh capital today.

book_subsections.title: Why Valuation Discipline Protects Capital
paragraphs: In cyclical manufacturing, paying 1.40 times book value feels harmless until you realize that a 6.48 percent return on capital earns less than a sovereign bond. Without a clear path to 12 percent ROCE, book value grows slowly and valuation multiples stay compressed.
Waiting for either stronger free cash flow or a deeper discount to tangible book value keeps the odds firmly on your side.
